transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
Just so tired all the time.
Could you tell me when you first started feeling this tired, how it came on, whether anything was going on around that time, and if you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?
It came on slowly, over about two months.
Could you tell me how much this tiredness is affecting your everyday life, and what medicines you're currently taking or have recently started or changed, including the doses if you know them?
I've had to stop my swimming.
Could you tell me about your past health, including any ongoing conditions, past illnesses, operations, or hospital stays?
I've had diabetes for years.
Have you ever had an allergy or a bad reaction to a medicine, or have you never had one, or are you not sure?
Yes, codeine makes me very sick.
How bad would you say the tiredness is: mild, moderate, or severe — or are you not sure?
I'd say about three out of ten.
What medicines are you taking these days — including anything new or recently changed — and do you know the doses?
Metformin, 500 mg twice a day.
Besides feeling tired, have you noticed anything else different or new going on?
I look after my husband, he's got Parkinson's.
Where in your body do you feel the tiredness most?
Nowhere in particular — just all over, really.
Is there anything that seems to make your tiredness better?
No, nothing seems to help it.
Along with the tiredness, have you noticed any other new changes or problems, or is it just the tiredness, or are you not sure?
I get more short of breath than usual on hills.
What worries you most about feeling tired and getting short of breath?
I worry I won't be able to keep caring for my husband.
How would you describe what the tiredness feels like for you?
Like I've just got no energy in me.
Besides your diabetes, is there anything else in your health history—like other long-term conditions, past illnesses, operations, or hospital stays—that you think would be helpful to mention?
I've got an underactive thyroid too.
Besides your diabetes and underactive thyroid, is there anything else about your past health—like other lasting conditions, past illnesses, operations, or hospital stays—that you’d like to mention?
No, nothing else I can think of.
Besides the Metformin 500 mg twice a day you mentioned, is there anything else you take for your health, including any new or recently changed medicines?
My husband's Parkinson's keeps me up some nights.
Along with the tiredness and getting more short of breath on hills, is there anything else you've noticed that you'd like to add?
Friends say I look pale.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
